decisions.reason: Step 2.1 left the initial index unspecified and 1/j is undefined at j=0. This is a nonfatal indexing defect: replacing radii and distance bounds by j+1 and 1/(j+1) yields closed bounded subsets of the open set covering it, so the null-union argument works. The mollified negative-part pairing, Holder limit, cutoff localization, and both-sign vanishing argument are valid under Countable Choice; the Statement is unchanged.

F3 and step 1.1 used e_m outside the standard-basis supplier, whose function-space coordinates are indexed by i<m. This nonfatal indexing error is repaired by using e_0,...,e_{m-1}, the corresponding lifts u_i, and sums over i<m throughout. Finite choice, bounded inverse on the finite-dimensional range, closed kernel, bounded projection, and the AC-based implicit-function graph and zero derivative now apply exactly. The Statement is unchanged.

F5 omitted its real-valued hypothesis, so the original identification of a possibly complex Rellich limit used a dependency outside its scope. This fatal dependency-citation gap is repaired without narrowing the Statement: use real tests, apply the real vanishing lemma separately to Re(u-w) and Im(u-w), and derive complex pairing bounds by real Holder on absolute values. Weak convergence identifies both pairings, and the reverse triangle inequality preserves the unit norm. AC supplies CC.

F2 originally suppressed the realization supplier chart hypotheses. Since its chart theorem requires m>=1, the reverse inclusion had a fatal dependency-citation gap at m=0. Step 1.2 now treats R^0 as the zero space and uses c(t)=u+th inside a ball in U; for m>=1 it first obtains the chart and then applies realization. Chain rule proves the forward inclusion in both cases. The Statement is unchanged, including the zero-constraint case.

F5 originally omitted m>=1 and was applied at m=0, a fatal dependency-citation gap; the contract also falsely said zero constraints were excluded. Step 2.1 now deduces DI(u)=0 from stationarity on ker DG(u)=X and uses the unique empty multiplier vector, while applying the common-kernel lemma only for m>=1. F6 explicitly relabels zero-based standard coordinates to the existing one-based component notation, fixing the e_m issue without changing the Statement.

The literal original refuted assertion named the compatible obstacle Definition, where psi^+ is always admissible; psi=1 fails that Definition. This fatal logical mismatch is repaired by explicitly refuting the unrestricted set formula after omitting Tpsi<=0, retaining the original trace-incompatibility contract and witness. Continuity on one-sided endpoint neighborhoods excludes v>=1 with zero trace, and truncation proves necessity for arbitrary real H1 interval data. No permitted obstacle is claimed to give an empty set.

The real obstacle set and real variational inequality do not allow u plus or minus i times a real cutoff. This fatal dependency-citation gap is repaired by restricting the variations to real tests and extending the resulting vanishing complex linearly, as the actual reaction Definition requires. Compact cutoffs, Radon inner regularity on the open noncontact set, and pointwise feasibility of continuous representatives then prove concentration and zero integral. F1/F2/Given now respect scalar fields; nonzero loci replace ambiguous support wording. The Statement is unchanged.

F7 reversed the null-set principle: 1_{0} vanishes on B minus {0} but has Dirac integral 1. This fatal dependency-citation error is repaired by observing that f-f(0) vanishes at the atom, so its absolute value integrates to zero on the null complement; hence integral f d(delta_0)=f(0). The loglog witness is L2 with L2 gradient and ACL off null exceptional lines, and two representatives with values 0/1 at the Lebesgue-null origin give distinct distribution pairings. Added direct radius rationalization and joining-circle null justification. The refuted interface is unchanged.
